texts.preamble: Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 -1- In The Court Of Sh. Vidya Prakash District Judge (Commercial Court)-02, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cnr No.: Dlnd010073942023 Cs (Comm.)/479/2023 In The Matter Of: - Ms. Neha Bajaj D/O Late Moti Ram Bajaj R/O H.No. 317/2, Paschim Puri, New Delhi ...Plaintiff Versus 1. Mr. Charan Preet Singh S/O Sh. Sardar Ajit Singh Shop Address-: At - Stall/ Shop No.1 Sector-12, Mini Market R.K.Puram, New Delhi 2. Mr. M.K. Tyagi S/O Sh. Sardar Ajit Singh Mob. 9971716128 3. Mr. B.C. Tyagi S/O Sh. Sardar Ajit Singh Both Are Residents Of: - H.No. 5-C, Rohtak Road Karol Bagh, New Delhi-110005 Mob. 9555168174 ...Defendants Date of Institution : 23-08-2023 Date of reserving Judgment : 20-02-2025 Date of pronouncement of Judgment : 27-02-2025 Cs (Comm.)/479/2023 Page 1 of 39 -2- Judgment
texts.facts: FACTS OF THE CASE: 2. The case of the plaintiff as set up in the plaint, in a nutshell, is as under: - 2.1 The plaintiff is the absolute owner and landlady of Stall No.1, including back portion of the Stall No.1, two side open, with roof, situated at Sector-12, Mini Market, R.K.Puram, New Delhi [hereinafter referred to as the 'Suit Property']. The detailed dimensions of the suit property are mentioned in the site plan in red colour marked as 'A' & 'B', which has been annexed with the plaint. 2.2 It is stated that the plaintiff is daughter of Sh. Surender Kumar Bajaj, who was real brother of Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj. Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj was the absolute owner of the suit property and he was employed in PEC Ltd. Company, New Delhi. The suit property was allotted to him by DDA on 28.03.1981. 2.3 It is averred that since Mr. Moti Ram Bajaj was not married during his life time, therefore, he had adopted the plaintiff, by way of an adoption deed executed between parents of the plaintiff namely Mrs. and Mr. Surender Bajaj and Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj (adopting father) on 24.3.1999 and since then, the plaintiff was living with her adoptive father Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj. 2.4 It is further averred that said Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj had unfortunately expired, leaving behind only one legal heir i.e. the plaintiff and thereafter, the plaintiff applied before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi to get a Succession Certificate of the movable and immovable properties of her deceased father namely Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj, wherein, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi had passed Succession order for succession certificate in favour of the plaintiff on 08.09.2005. Therefore, by virtue of said Succession Certificate, the plaintiff became absolute owner of the suit property. Subsequently, she applied and got installed electricity connection from BSES in her name in the suit property. 2.5 It is claimed that the defendants were misusing and stealing electricity by tapping the electricity wires directly from BSES Ltd. line. Besides, it is also claimed that the plaintiff has been continuously paying House Tax of the suit property. 2.6 It is averred that the suit property was let out for commercial use to defendant no.1 on monthly rent of 25,000/- excluding electricity, house tax and other charges on 08.10.2013. It was agreed between the parties that the defendant no.1 shall pay monthly rent of 25,000/- to the plaintiff, payable in one month advance, on or before 10th day of every month according to English Calendar month. Accordingly, the defendant no.1 paid rent up to October, 2016. Thereafter, the rent was increased by the plaintiff from 25,000/- to 30,000/- per month. Accordingly, the defendant no.1 paid rent to the plaintiff till October,2018. One cheque bearing no. 287178 dated 12.11.2018 for Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100375730/ 2 28,800/-, out of 30,000/-, was issued on account of rent for the month of November, 2018, but the said cheque was dishonoured on 13.11.2018 due to 'Funds Insufficient'. Therefore, it is claimed that the defendant no.1 is in arrears of rent to the tune of 1,80,000/- from November, 2018 to April, 2019. 2.7 It is further averred that on 15.12.2013, the defendant no.1 had also taken back portion of stall no.1 on monthly rent of 7,700/- per month, orally on same terms and conditions of the rent agreement dated 08th October, 2013, and subsequently, the rent in respect of said portion was also increased from 7,700/- per month to 8,400/- per month and the defendant no.1 paid increased rent @ 8,400/ - per month up to November, 2017 to the plaintiff. The defendant no.1 had also issued one cheque bearing no.789234 dated 20.12.2017 drawn on Indian Overseas Bank on account of rent for the month of December, 2017 in favour of the plaintiff, but the said cheque was also dishonoured on 19.12.2017 due to 'Funds Insufficient'. The plaintiff then filed a criminal complaint U/s 138 NI Act, qua the aforesaid two cheques against the defendant no.1.The plaintiff claims that the defendant no.1 is also in arrears of rent for back portion of the suit property from the month of December, 2017. 2.8 The plaintiff further avers that as per terms and conditions of the rent agreement, the defendant no.1 had also agreed that he would pay the electricity charges & water charges of the suit property in addition to the monthly rent, as per meter/sub meter reading and would also pay the maintenance charges directly to RWA/building/society maintenance charges, but, the plaintiff claims that the defendant no.1 neither paid the electricity consumption charges, nor paid any/maintenance charges to RWA/ building/ society, deliberately and intentionally. 2.9 It is alleged that the plaintiff came to know on 10.12.2018 that the defendant no.1 had clandestinely and mala fidely, and in breach of Clause 08 of the Lease Deed dated 08.10.2013, sub-let back portion/shop of the suit property to defendant nos. 2 &3 without her permission and prior consent in writing. Consequently, she got issued a legal notice dated 27.11.2018, thereby terminating the tenancy of defendant no.1 and called upon the said defendant and the sub-tenants of defendant no.1 to hand over the vacant and peaceful possession of the suit property to the plaintiff on or before midnight of December 26, 2018, failing which, it was informed that the defendants would be in unauthorized and illegal possession of the suit property, but to no avail. The plaintiff has further averred that in view of the provisions of Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, the tenancy of the defendant no.1 had come to an end after expiry of 30 days from the date of the legal notice expiring with the end of the month of the tenancy. 2.10 It is further averred that the defendants had also encroached upon the Government land to the extent of 6 x 11 ft. in width and this encroachment runs all along the side portion of the suit property. The portion shown as 6 ft. x 11 ft. is that portion of the land, which belongs to the Government and is shown and marked as green colour in the site plan, on which, the defendants have got no right, title or interest of any nature whatsoever. The plaintiff further claims that she had sent written complaints to the Deputy Commissioner of MCD, Green Park, New Delhi, BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. and also to Delhi Jal Board on 26.03.2019. Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100375730/ 3 2.11 The plaintiff further avers that after expiry of 30 days, the plaintiff made an oral request to defendant no.1 to vacate the suit property and despite such request, the defendant no.1 neither vacated the tenanted premises, nor got the same vacated from sub-tenants i.e. the defendant nos. 2 &3, nor paid the arrears of rent, nor deposited the electricity and other charges etc. till date, with mala fide intention. 2.12 The plaintiff further avers that the defendant no.1 had issued one cheque through his brother, vide cheque bearing no.290744 dated 30.11.2018 for 23440/- in favour of BSES for electricity consumption charges, but the said cheque got returned unpaid for reason ""Funds Insufficient" and legal representative of BSES got issued legal notice U/s 138 NI Act, against the plaintiff on 03.12.2018. 2.13 They are also using illegal connection of water. 2.14 It is further averred that the suit property is in illegal, unauthorized use and occupation of the defendants and that the suit property would easily fetch a rental income of at least 40,000/ - and 15,000/- per month, which is the prevalent market rate in the locality for same and similar accommodation for the last couple of years and therefore, the defendants are liable to pay mesne profit/ damages equal to rent. 3. On these facts and circumstances, the plaintiff has filed the present suit against the defendants praying therein, inter alia, a decree of possession/ejectment thereby directing them to hand over the physical and vacant possession of the suit property to the plaintiff, along with a decree for recovery of arrears of rent for the period from 10-11-2018 in respect of Stall No.1/ suit property @ 30,000/- per month and from December, 2017 @ 8,400/- per month [in respect of back portion of the stall no.1], along with interest @ 24% p.a., besides pendent-lite and future interest from date of filing of the present suit till its realization. Apart from same, a decree for recovery of mesne profits and damages and also compensation on account of sub-letting charges equivalent to market rate of rent @ 38,400/- p.m. of both the tenanted premises is also prayed for from the date of institution of the present suit till realization/ actual delivery of possession of the suit property, along with interest 18% per annum thereon. 4. On being served with the summons of the suit, the defendants put their appearance through counsels. Defendant nos. 2 and 3 filed their joint written statement on record contesting the suit. However, the defence of defendant no.1 was struck off, vide order dated 31-07-2024, passed by this Court, while considering the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as 'SCG Contracts India Pvt. Ltd. v. K. S. Chamankar Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.', reported in AIR 2019 SC 2691 and the fact that the said defendant had filed the written statement much beyond the maximum Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100375730/ 4 period of 120 days from 06.11.2023 i.e. when the defendant no.3 had appeared before the Court through video conferencing after being served with the summons of the suit. 5. In their joint written statement, the defendant nos.2 and 3 took various preliminary objections, inter alia, that:- 5.1 The plaintiff has no concern with the tenanted shop, which is totally situated independently on the back portion of the shop that belongs to the plaintiff and had given the same on rent to defendant no.1. Thus, it is stated that the plaint does not disclose any cause of action against them, which can be adjudicated only after measuring the area of the tenanted shop which belongs to the plaintiff, on the basis of relevant documents of the tenanted shop and the shop in possession of defendant no.2 does not fall within the said area of the tenanted shop, which belongs to the plaintiff. 5.2 The present suit has been filed by plaintiff in collusion with defendant no.1 in order to extort money from defendant no.2 and also to forfeit the security amount of 6,00,000/-, which was given by defendant No.2 to defendant no.1 when the property in question was rented out to defendant no.2 @ 12,000/- per month. However, the defendant no.1 had not issued any receipt for the same. The defendant no.3 was also searching a small shop for his elder brother i.e. defendant no.2 and after discussion, the area in possession of defendant no.2, was rented out by defendant no.1 to defendant no.2 and the said defendant paid a sum of 6,00,000/ - to defendant no.1 as security in the presence of his father and the rent of the tenanted shop/stall to defendant no.2 was fixed at the rate of 12,000/ - per month, including the electricity charges. 6. After 2-3 years, the defendant no.2 came to know that the area in his possession belongs to DDA or MCD, but the defendant no.1 always assured to him not to worry and if any problem or disturbance would arise, then he would refund the security amount of 6,00,000/- within one month or prior to eviction of the area in his possession. 7. Likewise, by way of Reply on Merits, the defendant nos. 2 and 3 have denied and controverted the averments made in corresponding Paras of the plaint. It is specifically denied that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of back portion of Stall-1 and thus, has no concern whatsoever with the shop in possession of defendant no.2. It may be noted that after framing the issues, while exercising the power conferred under Order XVA Rule 6(o) and (p) CPC, the Court had directed that the evidence shall be recorded by Ld. Local Commissioner, appointed by this Court on commission basis, vide said order dated 31-7-2024 (supra). Accordingly, the plaintiff and the defendant nos. 2 and 3 were directed to lead their respective evidence before Ld. Local Commissioner, in terms of the timeline/ scheduled framed therein. In pursuant thereto, the plaintiff has examined herself as PW1 before Ld. Local Commissioner. The proceedings dated 15-10-2024 of Ld. Local Commissioner would show that the plaintiff dropped PW2 namely Sh. Surender Bajaj, whose affidavit in evidence had already been filed on record, and closed her evidence on the said date. Accordingly, the aforesaid issue is decided against the said defendants and in favour of the plaintiff. The initial burden to prove issue no. 2 was placed upon defendant nos. 2 and 3, whereas, the initial burden to prove issue nos.5 and 9 was placed upon the plaintiff.
texts.arguments: The plaintiff has also averred that the defendants had tried to erect illegally some temporary construction at the roof of the suit property by covering the roof without prior consent or permission from any Govt. civic agency or from the plaintiff and her family members. 5.3 The plaintiff in collusion with defendant no.1, has filed the present suit despite the fact that the property in question which is in possession of defendant no.2, does not belong to the plaintiff and the defendant no.1, in collusion with the plaintiff, has cheated defendant no.2 and has taken the amount as stated above for security of the property in question in possession of defendant no.2 after impersonating himself as the owner and the plaintiff has no concern with the property in possession of defendant no.2 as the tenanted shop is completely different from the shop in possession of defendant no. 2 and there is no relationship between the plaintiff and the said defendants as landlord and tenant as the shop in their possession does not fall in the area of the tenanted shop. 5.4 It is reiterated that the shop in possession of the defendant no.2 is an independent shop, which is situated at the back portion of the tenanted shop, which belongs to the plaintiff and only the electricity supply is taken from the tenanted shop of the plaintiff and nothing more. 5.5 The plaint is liable to be dismissed on the ground of non-joinder of necessary parties i.e. DDA or MCD as the area in question is not covered in the area of shop of the plaintiff and the same either belong to MCD or DDA and MCD or DDA are the necessary and proper parties for adjudication of the present dispute. 5.6 It is further averred that the defendant no.3 is an Advocate by profession and the area, as stated, is portion of the suit property in the plaint and is in possession of Neha Bajaj vs Charan Preet Singh And Ors on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100375730/ 5 defendant no.2 and the defendant no.3 has no concern with the same and also, that the defendant no.3 is neither necessary, nor proper party in the present case and is liable to be deleted from the array of memo of parties. 5.7 The defendant no.2 was in the lawful possession of the back portion of the suit property and he was also issued Registration Certificate under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which was valid till 27.10.2021 and subsequently, Weights and Measures Department had also issued Certificate dated 16.03.2017 and the same was being re-evaluated from time to time. 5.8 It is further averred that the father of defendant no.1 namely Sh. Ajit Singh was involved in some civil and criminal matters and the defendant no.3, being an Advocate, was pursuing the matters on behalf of aforesaid Sh. Ajit Singh. Somewhere in the month of January 2015, the aforesaid Ajit Singh intimated that his son i.e. the defendant No.1 herein, is the owner of back portion of the tenanted shop, which is in his possession and he is willing to rent out the said back portion of the said tenanted shop. After referring to the pleadings of the parties and the evidence led by the plaintiff during trial, the first and foremost argument advanced on behalf of the plaintiff is that the defendants could not impeach the testimony of PW1 and since they chose not to lead any evidence from their side, the plaintiff has been able to prove her case. It has been contended that the plaintiff inherited the estate of her adoptive father namely Sh. Moti Ram Bajaj, by virtue of Succession Certificate granted vide order dated 08-09-2005 [Ex.PW1/C] in her favour by Hon'ble Delhi High Court. It has been further contended that the plaintiff has been regularly paying house tax in respect of suit premises, and has also been regularly paying electricity charges for the electricity connection installed therein. For this purpose, Ld. Counsel of plaintiff referred to and relied upon the relevant documents i.e. copies of electricity bills [Ex.PW1/D (Colly.)], copy of notice issued by BSES/ Electricity Department [Ex.PW1/E] and copies of House Tax Payment Receipts [Ex.PW1/F (Colly.)]. He, therefore, urged that all these issues should be decided in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant nos. 2 and 3. In support of his submissions, Ld. Counsel of plaintiff has also placed reliance upon decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case of 'Anita Jain v. Praveen Kumar Jain ' bearing RC. REV. 138/2022 decided on 06-01-2023. In the written arguments filed by defendant nos. 2 and 3, it is stated that the plaintiff has failed to establish any right, title or interest over the shop shown at point 'B' in the site plan. It is further stated that the plaintiff has not filed any allotment letter or possession letter in respect of said shop and such failure on the part of the plaintiff in producing said two foundational documents, undermines her claim regarding ownership over the said portion. It is further stated therein that the plaintiff has failed to disclose even the dimension of the shops shown in Site Plan [Ex.PW1/A], which would further show that the claims raised by plaintiff are baseless and not supported by any evidence. 33. In the aforesaid backdrop, it was incumbent upon the plaintiff to lead cogent and positive evidence showing that she is also the rightful owner of back portion termed as Shop at point 'B' in the Site Plan. In this backdrop, Hon'ble Delhi High Court while referring to S. 116 of Indian Evidence Act, as also to the relevant judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court on the point in issue, held that the tenant was estopped from challenging the ownership of the petitioner by virtue of principle of estoppel embodied in S. 116 of the said Act.
